rows.grounds: dual compound in genitive dual referring to bondage and liberation
abstract noun formed from the pair bondage and liberation

items.question: What is the status of bondage and liberation as a pair?
premises: Bondage and liberation are named together
Their pairing is treated as a single state
items.inference: The discourse treats bondage and liberation as a unified conceptual pair
items.plain_english: Bondage and liberation are spoken of as a single state of bondage-and-liberation.

rows.grounds: purpose of establishing sameness of all
purpose of defeating opponents in debate

items.question: For what purpose is the statement about bondage and liberation made?
premises: The statement serves universal equality
The statement serves defeating disputants
items.inference: The teaching is presented for establishing equality and refuting opponents
items.plain_english: This statement is made for the sake of universal equality and for striking down disputants.

rows.grounds: the state or nature of being Śiva
assert or maintain as a position
purpose of overcoming opponents in that debate

items.question: Why is the Śiva-nature of all beings not asserted in this context?
premises: Śiva-ness of beings is not claimed here
The aim is defeating disputants
items.inference: The non-assertion is strategic for refuting opponents rather than denying Śiva-ness
items.plain_english: They do not claim the Śiva-ness of all beings here, because the aim is to defeat those disputants.

rows.grounds: state of being identical with that reality
because bondage is absent in that state

items.question: Can bondage or liberation exist in the state of identity with that reality?
premises: In that selfhood bondage does not exist
Where bondage is absent liberation is not applicable
items.inference: Neither bondage nor liberation obtains in the state of that selfhood
items.plain_english: In that selfhood there is no bondage, and because of its absence there is no liberation either.

rows.grounds: liberation also, fused with particle api

items.question: Why can liberation not exist when bondage is absent?
premises: Bondage is absent in that state
Liberation depends on bondage as its correlate
items.inference: Liberation cannot exist without the presence of bondage
items.plain_english: Since bondage is absent, liberation, which depends on it, does not exist either.

items.question: What purpose does the Lord gain from knowledge arising through scripture?
premises: The Lord is already complete
Scripture produces knowledge
items.inference: Scriptural knowledge cannot serve a purpose for the Lord himself
items.plain_english: And what purpose indeed could the Lord have from knowledge gained through scripture?

items.question: For whose knowledge and for what purpose was scripture initiated?
premises: Scripture was begun by the Lord
Scripture aims at producing knowledge
items.inference: The initiation of scripture must be explained in terms of a beneficiary other than the Lord
items.plain_english: For what purpose did he begin the scripture, and for whose knowledge?

rows.grounds: as the agent of that activity

items.question: How should the Lord's agency in scripture be understood?
premises: He remains by his own will
He is the agent of that activity
items.inference: The Lord's role in scripture is to be known as free self-willed agency
items.plain_english: He indeed remains thus by his own will, and is to be known as the agent of that.

rows.grounds: comes to be or manifests as
devoted to carrying out that teaching

items.question: Who becomes the practitioner devoted to carrying out the teaching?
premises: The same self is the agent
Practice requires devoted engagement
items.inference: The same self manifests as the one intent on practicing the teaching
items.plain_english: He indeed would become the one intent on carrying out that practice.

rows.grounds: in the form of results such as wealth and desire

items.question: In what other forms does the same self manifest over time?
premises: The same self manifests as practitioner
Results like wealth and desire arise in time
items.inference: The same self also becomes the form of fruits such as wealth and desire at their proper time
items.plain_english: Likewise, he indeed also becomes, at the proper time, the form of fruits such as wealth, desire, and so on.

rows.grounds: states of being disputant and counter-disputant

items.question: Why do roles of proponent and opponent arise if he abides in that state?
premises: The self abides in its own state
Disputant roles appear in experience
items.inference: An explanation is required for the appearance of disputant roles within that abiding
items.plain_english: If he abides in that state, why then are there the roles of proponent and opponent?

rows.grounds: pertaining to the nature of reality

items.question: Does conventional usage ever define the true nature of reality?
premises: Own nature belongs to reality itself
Convention is a mode of usage
items.inference: Conventional usage never constitutes the intrinsic nature of things
items.plain_english: Know that own-nature belongs to reality itself; convention never does.

rows.grounds: nothing but the nature of consciousness
because it does not appear outwardly

items.question: Why is pure consciousness called a non-thing in the external sense?
premises: Reality is only consciousness-form
It does not manifest as an external object
items.inference: Consciousness is called a non-thing only because it lacks external objecthood
items.plain_english: It is only consciousness itself; because it does not manifest externally, it is called a non-thing.

items.question: How should everything be examined in the discussion that follows?
premises: All things are subject to examination
A single form provides the basis of inquiry
items.inference: Everything should be examined hereafter under one unifying form
items.plain_english: Everything that is to be examined should thus be considered hereafter under one single form.

rows.grounds: through association with results and their absence

items.question: What establishes the fitness of abiding in that state?
premises: Abiding in that state is under consideration
Fruit and non-fruit are connected to it
items.inference: The fitness of that abiding is established through its relation to fruit and non-fruit
items.plain_english: The fitness of abiding in that state is established by its connection with fruit and non-fruit.

rows.grounds: having the essence of Śiva as consciousness

items.question: What is the essential nature of whatever appears in experience?
premises: Things appear in experience
Appearance is not separate from consciousness
items.inference: Whatever appears is essentially consciousness in the form of Śiva
items.plain_english: Whatever appears is indeed of the nature of Śiva, whose form is consciousness.

rows.grounds: when the cause has a single nature
having the nature of a triad

items.question: Does a threefold nature contradict the unity of the cause?
premises: The cause is of one nature
A triadic character is attributed
items.inference: The threefold nature is not a fault when the cause remains one in essence
items.plain_english: When the cause is of one nature, its threefold character is not a fault.

rows.grounds: the intrinsic or inherent causal factor

items.question: What roles do will and its connection play as causes?
premises: That will is identified as the inherent cause
Its connection functions as auxiliary cause
items.inference: Will and its conjunction account for causality without dividing the one cause
items.plain_english: That will alone is the inherent cause, and its connection is the auxiliary cause.

rows.grounds: of all conventional dealings involving difference
having the nature of non-recognition of non-difference

items.question: What underlies all conventional dealings based on difference?
premises: Conventional usage involves distinctions
Non-difference is not recognized in such usage
items.inference: All difference-based convention rests on the non-recognition of non-difference
uncertainties: ākhyāti may imply non-apprehension or misapprehension depending on doctrinal context
items.plain_english: All conventional dealings involving difference have the form of non-recognition of non-difference.

rows.grounds: in earth and other such elements

items.question: Does conceptual imagination operate in that reality as it does in earth and other elements?
premises: Imagination operates in differentiated elements
That reality is being distinguished from them
items.inference: Conceptual imagination does not proceed in that reality as it does in earth and so on
items.plain_english: Imagination does not proceed in that reality as it does in earth and the like.

items.question: What status can imagination have when applied to what is truly real?
premises: Imagination constructs its objects
Truth is distinguished from imagined constructs
items.inference: Imagination has no ultimate standing in relation to what is truly real
items.plain_english: If that alone is imagined as such, what place can imagination have in what is truly real?

rows.grounds: in examples like a painted fire or aśoka tree

items.question: Where does imagination appear to have vivid effect despite lacking reality?
premises: Imagination lacks ultimate reality
Representations can still appear vivid
items.inference: Imagination shines only in limited cases such as painted fire or similar representations
items.plain_english: Imagination shines only in certain cases, such as a painted fire or an aśoka and the like.

items.question: How should the praise of such imagination be understood?
premises: Imagination was said to shine in limited cases
Calling it praiseworthy can be ironic
items.inference: The praise of imagination in such cases is meant as mockery
items.plain_english: To call it praiseworthy is, in fact, mockery.

rows.grounds: in the reality or principle of Śiva
for one who perceives or realizes
sameness or parity with imagined cases

items.question: Can imagined appearances be considered equal to direct experience of the Śiva principle?
premises: The Śiva principle can be directly experienced
Imagination operates only in limited representational cases
items.inference: For one who directly experiences the Śiva principle, imagined appearances have no equality with it
items.plain_english: For one who sees the Śiva principle through direct experience, there is no equality with mere imagination.
